title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence
hook: Documents pack meaning into layout, figures, and equations that plain text can't fully capture. Skip the OCR step: pretraining directly on rendered pages beats text-only pretraining.
key_points: Challenges the assumption that language models must be trained on text-only representations of documents and web pages.
Converting visually rich sources (figures, equations, page layout) into plain text for pretraining discards information text can't fully capture.
Studies unsupervised visual pretraining that learns directly from rendered visual documents, skipping text extraction entirely.
On the same underlying corpora, visual pretraining consistently beats text-only pretraining across multiple backbones and benchmarks.
Offers an efficient path to scalable language intelligence, using data pretraining pipelines currently discard.
content_html: Pretraining pipelines for language models usually start by stripping documents down to plain text — even when the source is a web page with figures, equations, or careful layout. This paper asks whether that's a mistake, studying what happens when a model pretrains directly on the visual rendering of documents instead of the OCR'd text.
extra_html: The authors run a systematic comparison of unsupervised visual pretraining against standard text-only pretraining, holding the underlying corpus fixed. Across several model backbones and benchmarks, the visually-pretrained models come out ahead, suggesting the layout and figures normally discarded during text extraction are themselves a useful learning signal. The authors position direct visual pretraining as a scalable, efficient path to stronger language intelligence, not just a bolt-on for multimodal models.

related.title: Unlimited OCR: Constant KV Cache for Long Documents
related.hook: LLM-based OCR slows down as documents get longer because the KV cache keeps growing. Unlimited OCR holds the cache constant, transcribing dozens of pages in one pass.

flashcards.prompt: What key assumption about language model pretraining does this paper challenge?
flashcards.back_html: That LMs must be trained on text-only representations. Converting documents to plain text discards figures, equations, and layout that carry meaning text alone can't capture.

flashcards.prompt: What pretraining approach did the authors find outperforms text-only pretraining on the same corpora?

choices.text: Unsupervised visual pretraining directly on rendered documents, no text extraction
Training only on OCR-extracted text with better tokenization
Doubling the amount of text-only training data

flashcards.explanation_html: Across backbones and benchmarks, visual pretraining on the same underlying corpora consistently beat text-only pretraining.

flashcards.prompt: Why can't converting a document to plain text fully preserve its information?
flashcards.back_html: Figures, typeset equations, and page layout carry meaning that plain-text extraction discards or can't faithfully represent.

flashcards.prompt: What's the practical implication of this study for scaling language intelligence?

choices.text: Visual pretraining on documents offers an efficient path to scale beyond text-only data
Visual data is a distraction and should be filtered out of pretraining corpora
Only multimodal chat models benefit; base language models see no gain

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper frames direct visual pretraining as a scalable, efficient path to language intelligence, not just a multimodal add-on.
